newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold closes lower, silver steady.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold closes lower, silver steady.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees lower at 4,705 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,740 rupees as higher arrivals of smuggled gold dragged prices lower towards the close after a steady start.
** Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 300 rupees lower at 55,100 rupees per piece after losing 150 rupees on Tuesday.
** Silver (.999) closed steady at 6,840 rupees per kg as sluggish industrial buying and a fresh slide in the world market trimmed early gains in the local market towards the close.

Gold 24 carat closed 35 rupees lower at 4,705 rupees per 10 gramme against the previous close of 4,740 rupees as higher arrivals of smuggled gold dragged local prices lower towards the close after a steady start, dealer said.
Gold was down by 15 rupees per 10 gramme on Tuesday.
"Smugglers are trying to bring as much gold as possible in India before the monsoon and we are witnessing more arrivals of imported gold through unofficial channels in the market," dealers said.
Prices of a gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closed 300 rupees lower at 55,100 rupees per piece after losing 150 rupees per piece on Tuesday.
"Sluggish seasonal buying and sliding global prices also aided the subdued sentiment for gold today," said Mahavir Shah, a leading dealer.
Silver (.999) closed steady at 6,840 rupees per kg as a new slide in the world market trimmed early gains near the close. Silver was up by 10 rupees per kg on Tuesday.
"Setback in the gold prices also subdued the silver market during the day," Shah said.
